Adding the digital version of a driver's licence to iPhone's features looks set to expand to a 15th US state in the near term.

Apple currently lists 14 states, along with the territory of Puerto Rico, that support this feature, and backend resources now indicate one more state is about to be added...

Many of us have long hoped that one day we could ditch physical forms of identification like driver's licences and passports and just present a digital ID via our iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be a long way off, but Apple took its first step back in 2021 when it announced plans to let iPhone users add their driver's licences or state IDs to the Wallet app. So far, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend resources spotted by MacRumors indicate that Oklahoma is about to join the list.

We've previously detailed the steps needed to add a driver's licence or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. As we noted at the time, bear in mind that a digital ID is not a complete replacement for the physical document, so sadly we'd still recommend you continue to carry the physical version with you.

That said, the digital version is useful when it comes to protecting your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints, as well as when proof of age is required when dealing with a merchant. The ID can confirm that you meet the age requirement, but won't disclose any personal information, such as date of birth.
